data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A checklist is an explicit, human-readable artifact, whereas a model's mapping is an opaque, distributed representation, so the confound runs in opposite directions (checklist confounds with human reasoning; model confounds with the training distribution).","The panel can introspect and report on extra-checklist reasoning, while a model cannot introspect on its mapping, so the evaluation strategies available are different.","The checklist is fixed and shared; the model's mapping is individual and learned, so aggregation interacts differently with the confound."],"overturn_conditions":["It is shown that the panel cannot or does not apply extra-checklist reasoning, so the confound is absent.","It is shown that checklist-conformant and intelligence-conformant answers are always the same, so no evaluation can separate them.","It is shown that the evaluation measures reasoning traces well enough to attribute accuracy to the correct source even in the presence of the confound."],"shared_structure":["Both concern an explicit procedure applied by agents who also carry an implicit reasoning capacity that can override or supplement the procedure.","Both face the question of whether observed accuracy is due to the explicit procedure or the implicit capacity.","Both predict that the explicit procedure's contribution is confounded with the implicit capacity unless the evaluation separates them."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_008"],"transfer_claims":["The methodology for distinguishing 'the explicit procedure did the work' from 'the implicit capacity did the work' transfers: probe the system with items where the two diverge and see which one the system tracks.","If the panel tracks the checklist even when extra-checklist reasoning would give a different answer, the checklist is doing the work; if the panel overrides the checklist, the panel's intelligence is doing the work.","The distinction is evaluable in a single evaluation only if the evaluation includes items that separate checklist-conformant from intelligence-conformant answers."]},"claim":"If the panel can apply extra-checklist reasoning that restores accuracy on adversarial items where the checklist's surface cues fail, then a single evaluation cannot cleanly attribute the panel's reliability to the checklist rather than to panel-level\u8865\u4e01 reasoning, so the compliance-vs-genuine distinction is confounded by the panel's own intelligence.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The evaluation measures intermediate reasoning traces, so extra-checklist reasoning is detectable and the confound can be controlled.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The panel is rigorously trained to apply only the checklist and nothing else, so extra-checklist reasoning is suppressed by design.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The adversarial items are designed so that extra-checklist reasoning is also misled, eliminating the compensatory pathway.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is so detailed that there is no room for extra-checklist reasoning, making the confound vacuous.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Suppose adversarial items are introduced and the panel still gets them right. One explanation is that the checklist encodes genuine structure and the panel faithfully applies it. Another is that the checklist is a surface heuristic, the panel notices the surface cues are misleading, and applies extra-checklist reasoning to compensate. Both produce the same accuracy. The single evaluation cannot distinguish them unless it also controls for or measures the panel's extra-checklist reasoning. This is a confound: the panel's own intelligence acts as an unmeasured mediator between checklist compliance and outcome accuracy.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
